record.context_brief: Rayleigh polynomials and log-concave diagonal coefficients
record.original_question:
If f ∈ R[z1, ..., zn] is a Rayleigh multi-affine polynomial and
Δ(f)(t) = Σ_{k=0}^n (n choose k) c_k t^k is its diagonal
specialization, then the coefficient sequence (c_k) should be
log-concave and have no internal zeros.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f \in \mathbb{R}[z_1, \dots, z_n]$ be a multi-affine polynomial (i.e. of degree at most one in each variable) with nonnegative coefficients. Say that $f$ is Rayleigh if for every $i \neq j$ and every $x = (x_1,\dots,x_n) \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^n$,
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial z_i}(x) \cdot \frac{\partial f}{\partial z_j}(x) \;\geq\; f(x) \cdot \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial z_i \partial z_j}(x).$$
Define the diagonal specialization of $f$ to be the univariate polynomial obtained by substituting $z_1 = z_2 = \cdots = z_n = t$, written in the form
$$\Delta(f)(t) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} c_k\, t^k.$$
Prove or disprove: for every Rayleigh multi-affine polynomial $f$, the sequence $(c_0, c_1, \dots, c_n)$ is log-concave (i.e. $c_k^2 \geq c_{k-1} c_{k+1}$ for $1 \leq k \leq n-1$) and has no internal zeros (i.e. its support is an interval of integers).
artifact.status_search_result: The diagonal log-concavity conjecture for Rayleigh multi-affine polynomials (attributed to Wagner and to Borcea–Brändén) is known to hold for the stronger class of strongly Rayleigh (equivalently real stable) polynomials, since their diagonal specializations are real-rooted (and thus log-concave with no internal zeros) — a fact subsumed by the theory of Lorentzian polynomials of Brändén–Huh. For general Rayleigh polynomials a definitive resolution was not located: related stronger statements (e.g. log-concavity of the rank sequence of Rayleigh measures) are known to fail, but the diagonal version specifically has not been verified as solved in the searched sources.

status_evidence.title: Lorentzian polynomials (Brändén–Huh)
status_evidence.snippet: Lorentzian polynomials unify strong/complete log-concavity for homogeneous polynomials; real stable polynomials are Lorentzian after normalization, so their diagonal specializations are log-concave.
status_evidence.claim: For strongly Rayleigh (real stable) multi-affine polynomials the diagonal log-concavity conclusion is known.

status_evidence.title: Negative dependence and the geometry of polynomials (Borcea–Brändén–Liggett)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces strongly Rayleigh measures and discusses log-concavity properties; certain rank-sequence log-concavity statements for Rayleigh measures are disproved.
status_evidence.claim: Some log-concavity statements for general Rayleigh measures fail, but the diagonal-specialization conjecture is not declared solved.
